examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Identify whether a recurrence reduces n by a constant, a ratio, or a nonlinear transform. Master theorem requires its stated form and hypotheses. Normalize by an expected leading factor in expressions such as T(n)=√nT(√n)+n; substituting log n can expose the true depth.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
T(1)=1 and T(n)=2T(n/2)+n for powers of two. Find T(8).

**Answer: 32.** T(2)=4; T(4)=12; T(8)=32. In general T(n)=n(1+log₂n), giving Θ(n log n). Each of the log₂n nonleaf levels contributes n work, and leaves contribute n.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Master theorem does not directly apply to T(n−1) or T(√n). Fit initial conditions before discarding characteristic-root terms.

Do not apply the Master theorem to T(n)=T(n−1)+n.
